newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand ANZ unit's H1 profit edges up.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand ANZ unit's H1 profit edges up.

text.p: ANZ Banking Group's New Zealand operations reported a profit of NZ$78.6 million after taxes and minority interests for the half-year to March 31, and noted that this reflected a small rise over the year-ago period at the same time as total income dipped.

"It is a very good result in an intensely competitive market," the bank's local managing director David Airey said in a statement of the results, which followed an interim report by its Australian-based parent earlier in the day.
The profit rose by 2.48 percent compared with the year-ago period, and accompanied a 10.93 percent drop in net interest income to $241.3 million.
"This was due to lower margins and a modification of capital structure in September 1996," Airey noted.
Total operating expenses at $319.4 million remained steady compared with both the year-ago and preceding half-years.
While he anticipated further growth in the business, Airey also predicted that more branches would be closed in New Zealand, after the closure of 34 during the period.
Consumer preference for electronic transactions continued to grow and as a result more of the remaining 225 branches would be closed over the coming 18 months, he said.

"Customers now require a much wider range of distribution channels. In addition to electronics, we are meeting the need through major increases in the use of telephone banking and mobile managers, and an increasingly sales-oriented branch network," Airey added.
